default_source.note: Written by the MENDORA development team from general home-maintenance knowledge. Not reviewed or certified by a licensed professional.

entries.title: Slow-draining sink or basin
clarifying_questions: Is only one sink slow, or are other drains in the home slow too?
Did it start suddenly or get worse over time?

possible_causes.title: Build-up in the trap (U-bend)
possible_causes.explanation: Grease, food, soap or hair can collect in the curved pipe under the sink.

possible_causes.title: Blocked drain stopper or strainer
possible_causes.explanation: Hair and debris often catch on the plug or strainer at the top of the drain.

possible_causes.title: Blockage further along the waste pipe
possible_causes.explanation: If several drains are slow, the problem may be in a shared pipe.

next_steps: Remove and clean the sink strainer or pop-up plug if it lifts out by hand.
Try a sink plunger, with a little water in the sink to make a seal.
If several drains are slow or water backs up into another fixture, stop and contact a plumber.
safety_restrictions: Don't mix drain-cleaning chemicals, or use them together with a plunger — splashes can burn skin and eyes.

entries.title: Dripping tap
clarifying_questions: Does the water drip from the spout or from around the handle?
Is it the hot tap, the cold tap, or a mixer?

possible_causes.title: Worn washer or O-ring
possible_causes.explanation: Rubber seals inside the tap wear out over time and stop sealing fully.

possible_causes.title: Worn cartridge (mixer taps)
possible_causes.explanation: Single-lever taps use a cartridge that can wear or crack.

possible_causes.title: Damaged valve seat
possible_causes.explanation: The surface the washer presses against can become rough.

next_steps: Check whether the drip comes from the spout or the handle — this helps a plumber identify the part.
Place a bowl under the tap and note the tap type and brand if visible.
Replacing washers or cartridges needs the water supply isolated; if you're not confident doing that, contact a plumber.
safety_restrictions: Hot taps can scald — let water cool and isolate the supply before anyone works on the tap.

entries.title: Toilet keeps running after flushing
symptoms: Water keeps running into the bowl
clarifying_questions: Does the water stop if you gently lift the float?
Is water overflowing from the cistern or onto the floor?

possible_causes.title: Worn flush valve seal (flapper)
possible_causes.explanation: If the seal at the bottom of the cistern leaks, water trickles into the bowl.

possible_causes.title: Float set too high
possible_causes.explanation: The fill valve keeps running if the float doesn't shut it off in time.

possible_causes.title: Faulty fill valve
possible_causes.explanation: A worn valve may not close fully.

next_steps: Lift the cistern lid and check whether the chain or flush mechanism is caught.
Watch whether water flows into the overflow pipe — that suggests the float level needs adjusting.
If water is spilling onto the floor, turn off the toilet's isolation valve if you can reach it, and contact a plumber.
safety_restrictions: The cistern lid is heavy and breakable — put it down flat on a towel.

entries.title: Blocked toilet
symptoms: Toilet bowl fills up and drains slowly
clarifying_questions: Are other drains (shower, sink) also backing up?
Is sewage or dirty water coming out anywhere?

possible_causes.title: Blockage in the toilet trap
possible_causes.explanation: Too much paper or items that shouldn't be flushed can block the bend in the toilet.

possible_causes.title: Blockage in the main drain
possible_causes.explanation: If other drains back up too, the shared drain may be blocked.

next_steps: Don't flush again — it can make the bowl overflow.
Try a toilet (flange) plunger with steady, gentle pushes.
If other drains are backing up or sewage appears, stop and contact a plumber.
safety_restrictions: Wear gloves, and wash hands well afterwards. Keep children away from dirty water.

entries.title: Low water pressure at one tap
clarifying_questions: Is the low pressure at one tap only, or throughout the home?
Is it hot water, cold water, or both?

possible_causes.title: Blocked aerator
possible_causes.explanation: The small mesh at the end of the spout can collect limescale and grit.

possible_causes.title: Partly closed isolation valve
possible_causes.explanation: A valve on the pipe under the sink may not be fully open.

possible_causes.title: Supply issue
possible_causes.explanation: If every tap is affected, the cause may be the main supply or a tank.

next_steps: If the aerator unscrews by hand, clean the mesh and refit it.
Check whether other taps in the home are affected.
If the whole home has low pressure, check with neighbours or your water supplier before calling a plumber.

entries.title: Small drip under a sink
symptoms: Small drip from pipes under the sink
Water in a bowl under the trap
clarifying_questions: Is it a slow drip or a steady stream?
Is any water near sockets, plugs or appliances?

possible_causes.title: Loose waste-pipe joint
possible_causes.explanation: Plastic waste fittings can work loose over time.

possible_causes.title: Worn seal in the trap
possible_causes.explanation: The rubber seal inside a trap joint may be worn or misaligned.

possible_causes.title: Leaking supply connection
possible_causes.explanation: A drip from the flexible hoses or valves feeding the tap.

next_steps: Place a bowl underneath and dry the pipes so you can see where the drip starts.
Check whether it drips only when the sink is draining (waste pipe) or all the time (supply pipe).
A drip from a supply hose or valve, or any steady flow, should be checked by a plumber.
safety_restrictions: If water is near sockets or appliances, don't touch them — this becomes an electrical safety issue.

entries.title: No hot water from the water heater
symptoms: Water heater or geyser doesn't heat
clarifying_questions: Is the water heater electric or gas?
Is its power switch or indicator light on?

possible_causes.title: Heater switched off or its breaker tripped
possible_causes.explanation: Electric heaters often have a separate switch or breaker.

possible_causes.title: Thermostat set too low
possible_causes.explanation: The temperature setting may have been turned down.

possible_causes.title: Failed heating element or thermostat
possible_causes.explanation: These parts wear out and need replacing by a professional.

next_steps: Check that the heater's wall switch is on and its indicator light (if any) is lit.
Check whether its breaker has tripped. Reset a tripped breaker once only — if it trips again, stop and call an electrician.
Repairs inside a water heater need a qualified plumber or electrician. Gas heaters need a registered gas engineer.
entries.professional_reason: Water heaters work with high temperatures, pressure and electricity or gas.
safety_restrictions: Never open the water heater's cover or adjust its safety valves.
Gas water heaters: if you smell gas, leave the area and call the gas emergency line.

entries.title: Light bulb not working
clarifying_questions: Is it one light, or several lights at once?
Is the bulb holder or fitting cracked, scorched or loose?

possible_causes.title: Blown bulb
possible_causes.explanation: The most common cause when a single light stops working.

possible_causes.title: Loose bulb
possible_causes.explanation: A bulb that isn't fully screwed or clipped in may not connect.

possible_causes.title: Fault in the fitting or circuit
possible_causes.explanation: If a new bulb doesn't work, the fault is elsewhere and needs an electrician.

next_steps: Switch the light off and let the bulb cool before touching it.
Replace the bulb with one of the same type, fitting and wattage.
If the new bulb doesn't work, or several lights are out, contact an electrician.
safety_restrictions: Use a stable step stool, not a chair.
If the fitting is cracked, scorched or loose, leave it switched off and call an electrician.

entries.title: Flickering light
clarifying_questions: Does one light flicker, or several lights in the home?
Does it flicker when a large appliance switches on?

possible_causes.title: Loose or failing bulb
possible_causes.explanation: A bulb nearing the end of its life, or not seated properly, can flicker.

possible_causes.title: Dimmer not compatible with the bulb
possible_causes.explanation: Some LED bulbs flicker on dimmer switches.

possible_causes.title: Loose connection or circuit problem
possible_causes.explanation: If several lights flicker, the cause may be in the wiring — this needs an electrician.

next_steps: With the light switched off and cool, check the bulb is fitted firmly, or try a new bulb of the same type.
If the bulb is on a dimmer, check whether the bulb is marked as dimmable.
If several lights flicker, or you hear buzzing, contact an electrician.
safety_restrictions: Buzzing, heat or a burning smell means stop and call an electrician.

entries.title: Breaker or trip switch tripped
symptoms: Power went off in part of the home
A switch in the fuse box is down
clarifying_questions: Does it trip again straight after resetting it?
Did it trip when a particular appliance was switched on?

possible_causes.title: Overloaded circuit
possible_causes.explanation: Too many high-power appliances on one circuit at the same time.

possible_causes.title: Faulty appliance
possible_causes.explanation: An appliance with a fault can trip the safety switch.

possible_causes.title: Wiring fault
possible_causes.explanation: If it keeps tripping with appliances unplugged, the wiring needs an electrician.

next_steps: Unplug or switch off appliances on the affected circuit.
With dry hands, reset the tripped switch once.
If it trips again, leave it off and contact an electrician. Never hold or force a breaker on.
safety_restrictions: Only touch the fuse box with dry hands, standing on a dry floor.
Never remove the fuse box cover.

entries.title: Socket not working
symptoms: Nothing works when plugged into one socket
clarifying_questions: Do other sockets in the same room work?
Is the socket cracked, discoloured or warm?

possible_causes.title: Tripped breaker or trip switch
possible_causes.explanation: Check the fuse box for a switch that is down.

possible_causes.title: Faulty appliance or plug
possible_causes.explanation: The appliance itself may be the problem.

possible_causes.title: Faulty socket or wiring
possible_causes.explanation: Needs a qualified electrician to check and repair.

next_steps: Plug in a different appliance you know works to test the socket.
Check the fuse box for a tripped switch.
If the socket still doesn't work, leave it unused and contact an electrician.
entries.professional_reason: Repairs to sockets and their wiring must be done by a qualified electrician.
safety_restrictions: Never open a socket.
A cracked, discoloured, warm or buzzing socket should not be used at all.

entries.title: Light switch not working
symptoms: Switch doesn't turn the light on
clarifying_questions: Does a new bulb work in that light?
Is the switch warm, cracked or making noise?

possible_causes.title: Blown bulb
possible_causes.explanation: Rule out the bulb first.

possible_causes.title: Worn switch
possible_causes.explanation: Switches wear out mechanically over time.

possible_causes.title: Loose connection
possible_causes.explanation: Needs an electrician — loose connections can overheat.

next_steps: Try a new bulb of the same type in the light first.
Check the fuse box for a tripped switch.
If it still doesn't work, contact an electrician — replacing a switch involves live wiring.
safety_restrictions: Never take the switch off the wall.
Stop using a switch that is warm, crackling or scorched.

entries.title: Door sticks or rubs
symptoms: Door rubs on the frame or floor
clarifying_questions: Where does it rub — top, side or bottom?
Did it start in damp weather?

possible_causes.title: Loose hinge screws
possible_causes.explanation: A loose top hinge lets the door drop and rub.

possible_causes.title: Wood swelling from humidity
possible_causes.explanation: Wooden doors can swell in damp weather.

possible_causes.title: Building movement
possible_causes.explanation: If cracks appear around the frame, the cause may be structural — get it checked.

next_steps: Check whether the hinge screws are loose and tighten them with a screwdriver.
Look for a shiny worn spot to see exactly where it rubs.
If the door rubs after the hinges are tight, a carpenter can plane or adjust it.
safety_restrictions: Doors are heavy — don't take one off its hinges on your own.

entries.title: Loose hinge or sagging door
clarifying_questions: Do the screws tighten, or do they keep turning?
Is the wood around the hinge split?

possible_causes.title: Screws worked loose
possible_causes.explanation: Regular use loosens hinge screws over time.

possible_causes.title: Stripped screw holes
possible_causes.explanation: If screws keep turning, the hole is worn and won't grip.

possible_causes.title: Damaged hinge
possible_causes.explanation: A bent or cracked hinge needs replacing.

next_steps: Tighten the hinge screws with the right size screwdriver.
If a screw keeps turning, a carpenter can fill the hole or fit a longer screw.
Replace a bent or cracked hinge with the same size and type.
safety_restrictions: Support heavy doors while working on hinges.

entries.title: Squeaky door hinge
symptoms: Door squeaks or creaks when opened
clarifying_questions: Is the squeak from the hinge, or from the door rubbing?

possible_causes.title: Dry hinge
possible_causes.explanation: Hinges squeak when they lack lubrication.

possible_causes.title: Rust or dirt in the hinge
possible_causes.explanation: Build-up inside the hinge causes friction.

next_steps: Wipe the hinge clean.
Apply a small amount of household lubricant to the hinge, and open and close the door a few times.
Wipe away any excess so it doesn't drip onto the floor.

entries.title: Drawer sticks or won't close
symptoms: Drawer is hard to open or close
clarifying_questions: Is the drawer wooden with wooden runners, or does it have metal slides?
Is something caught behind it?

possible_causes.title: Item caught behind the drawer
possible_causes.explanation: Something may have fallen behind or under it.

possible_causes.title: Worn or dry runners
possible_causes.explanation: Wooden runners wear; metal slides can get dirty or bent.

possible_causes.title: Loose drawer front or runner screws
possible_causes.explanation: Screws can work loose over time.

next_steps: Empty the drawer, take it out if it lifts out easily, and check for anything caught.
Clean the runners, and tighten any loose runner screws.
Rub a little candle wax on wooden runners so they slide more easily.
safety_restrictions: On tall chests of drawers, don't open several full drawers at once — the unit can tip.

entries.title: Wobbly chair or table
clarifying_questions: Is a joint loose, or is one leg shorter or the floor uneven?
Is the wood cracked anywhere?

possible_causes.title: Loose joint or screws
possible_causes.explanation: Joints loosen with use.

possible_causes.title: Uneven leg or floor
possible_causes.explanation: One leg may be slightly shorter, or the floor may be uneven.

possible_causes.title: Cracked leg or rail
possible_causes.explanation: A crack weakens the furniture and needs repair.

next_steps: Turn it over and tighten any loose screws or bolts.
Try it on a different spot of floor to see if the floor is uneven.
If wood is cracked, stop using it and ask a carpenter to repair it.
safety_restrictions: Don't stand on a wobbly chair or stool.
